title: Which key signs the delegation?
summary: Before any agent can act on a request in Dinis's name, the delegation to decisions.d must be signed by a key only Dinis holds. Which key is it?

beats.narration: You asked for one agent that can issue requests as you, under a limited power you sign. Everything rests on the key you sign it with.
Your key in this repository's person-keys file was made by an agent, conductor@, which keeps the private half too. So it cannot stand for your word.

Your record on pki.sgit.ai is the register's anchor, made in your browser. pki.sgit.ai already supports an agent operated by a person: an operates link with an end date and a policy, withdrawn when you choose.
If you say yes, decisions.d makes its record there. It asks for your operates link only after counsel.d drafts the power and security@ reviews the design, on Monday at the earliest.

decision.question: Is your pki.sgit.ai anchor key (dinis.cruz, sha256:db7f79fdd87e030a) the key you will sign the delegation with?

options.label: Yes, the pki.sgit.ai anchor key
good: Delegation, expiry and withdrawal already exist there
One verifier for statements and requests
bad: Every receiver must reach pki.sgit.ai to check
Your device and passkey become the single point of trust

options.label: A new key made on your device for this only
bad: A new key to publish, pin and verify
Its link to you must still be proved
blocks: A new key and its publication

options.label: Not yet
good: Nothing changes until counsel.d and security@ have looked
bad: Decisions keep waiting on your sessions

decision.why: It is the only published key of yours that no agent holds, and pki.sgit.ai already models a limited, expiring, revocable delegation.
